heading: Compare the setting you will actually visit
intro: Cuyabeno’s flooded waterways and lagoon setting are described in IUCN’s regional account; UNESCO describes Yasuní’s humid tropical forest. These are useful starting points for imagining a journey, but they are not complete descriptions of every visitor program. Ask each provider for the location of the accommodation and activities before deciding how much of that regional picture applies to your stay. A Napo-corridor proposal also needs a clear explanation of its relationship to Yasuní National Park. Compare the actual map, not only the place name. If a lodge is outside the park, that fact should be clear without implying the experience has no value.
points: Where are the accommodation and outings located?
Is the proposed base inside or outside the national park?
Which regional description applies to this specific stay?

heading: Compare the balance of river and forest time
intro: Look at how each itinerary divides your time between travel, guided observation and rest. For a Cuyabeno proposal, ask which waterways and lagoon outings are actually included. For a Yasuní or Napo proposal, ask which forest and river activities the specific base offers. Neither regional name establishes your schedule. Put both daily programs beside one another and mark the full activity periods. Ask how an outing may change with local conditions and what the alternative would involve. If you enjoy slow observation, a clearly described pause can matter more than another activity title. If walking is important, discuss the actual terrain and pace before accepting the program.
points: Which river and forest activities does each program include?
How much observation time remains after transfers?
What alternatives are discussed if an outing changes?

heading: Compare interpretation before species lists
intro: UNESCO’s Yasuní account records a range of mammals and birds; it is regional evidence, not an itinerary promise. The same distinction matters when a Cuyabeno provider shows a wildlife gallery. Ask how observations from the proposed area are recorded, who guides the outings and how the guide explains uncertain identifications. Share birding or photography interests as interests rather than a demand for a guaranteed encounter. Compare the language, group arrangement and time to observe. A journey can remain worthwhile when a target animal stays unseen if you enjoy the setting and interpretation. Do not rank the regions by the most dramatic photograph or assume a longer checklist describes your own short visit.
points: Who guides the activities and in which language?
What observations are documented for the proposed area?

heading: Compare comfort at the property level
intro: A region cannot settle your room preferences. Request the room arrangement, bathroom details, meals and any communications or power arrangements that affect your choice from each actual property. Mark what is confirmed, what is requested and what remains unanswered. Explain mobility, balance, dietary or equipment requirements early so the provider can assess the specific plan. Compare boarding and trail demands alongside accommodation rather than judging suitability from the room alone. Ask which activities are shared and which, if any, are private for your booking. If the answer refers to a different property or a general lodge category, return to the precise proposal. A clear reply is more useful than a broad comfort label.
points: What room and meal arrangements are confirmed?
How do boarding and trail demands fit our group?
Which activities are shared or private for this booking?

heading: Compare the complete journey and quote
intro: Start both comparisons at your real departure point and end them where your next travel plans begin. Ask for the full transfer sequence, meeting points, responsibility for each segment and timing for your dates. Count nights and the activity time left after arrival and before departure. Keep the quote beside that schedule, including accommodation, meals, guiding, excursions, equipment and optional items. Do not assume one region is always cheaper or easier to reach; the actual proposal determines the comparison. Check the current official regional advice for gateways and transfers as well as the destination. Ask the provider to clarify any route change, without treating a general itinerary as confirmation that the route is suitable for your dates.
points: What is the complete outward and return sequence?
Which transfers and services are included in the total quote?
How would a change affect the onward journey?

heading: Choose the clearer fit for your priorities
intro: Write down your three most important priorities and score each proposal against the same questions. You might focus on water-based observation, guiding language, activity time, physical demands or the arrangement of the stay. Use written answers rather than a destination’s reputation to fill in the comparison. If one proposal leaves an essential requirement unresolved, ask for clarification before accepting it. If both fit, compare the complete price and change terms alongside the experience you prefer. There is no universal winner for every traveller, and visiting both regions is not necessary to justify a first Amazon stay. A coherent program with a base you understand can be a better fit than adding transfers simply to collect both names.
points: Can the provider clarify each essential requirement in writing?
What are the payment, modification and cancellation terms?
Who is responsible for the final itinerary and communication?
